key_findings: The Android rating dialog is a sentiment gate. It asks Enjoying Example Workout Log? first and sends No answers to a feedback form, which Google Play's in-app review guidance forbids. Remove the question and the routing in the next release.

Both platforms ask at launch on the 3rd launch and from a Settings button that calls the review API. Move the prompt to the workout summary screen and replace the button with a link to the store's review page.
6.3.0 made ratings worse on both stores: low-star share rose to 40.4% on the App Store (z 3.02) and 43.1% on Google Play (z 3.66). Sync or data loss is the top theme (15 and 17 low-star reviews).

6.4.0 is better than 6.3.0 on both stores (App Store 20.8%, z -2.11; Google Play 21.6%, z -2.39) but still short of the target: App Store 3.83 against 4.1, Google Play 3.8 against 3.9, a gap to measure again on the first version without the Android dialog.

android_gate_note: Google Play's average went from 3.92 on 6.1.0 to 4.32 on 6.2.0, the version that added the dialog (z -1.02, no clear change). A rise that starts with a gate is not evidence of a better app. 6.2.0 to 6.4.0 all ran the dialog, so the Google Play target comes from 6.1.0 only, and the first version without the dialog becomes the new baseline.
